lesson: After a successful supported relay, one receiving jaw frame crossed a joint wrap and the other exceeded the continuity limit at coarse samples. Repreview with a smaller0.07-rad maximum joint step; retain the unchanged continuity and table guards. Never accept the wrapping branch merely because its end pose is reachable.

Using the deep grasp-pad anchor on a thin block put distal fingertips below the tabletop and correctly failed preflight before action. Use the public distal finger geometry for a shallow supported grip; never disable tabletop clearance.
Keep the T supported by the table throughout rotation and sliding; a pick-and-place solution violates this task. Grip the narrow stem, compare jaw frames and preview complete planar paths.
The long axis of a T is directed, not symmetric: match the crossbar and stem end separately. Observe after release and correct using current images. Joint arrival is not official success.
When one arm cannot reach both ends, slide to a visible central relay area, release on the table, park, and reobserve before the other arm continues. Reserve both-arm homing inside the native budget.
